# Ecommerce Platform Support

`customer_support.model.b2b.ecommerce_platform` · vertical · parent `customer_support.model.b2b`

> Supporting merchants who sell through our platform. The customer is a business whose revenue passes through our uptime, and three things follow from that. Severity is denominated in the merchant's money and they can compute it. A checkout fault is not "a degraded experience", it is an hourly figure the merchant will quote in the ticket, in the escalation and in the renewal conversation. Any triage model that ranks by user count rather than by transaction exposure will systematically under-serve the merchants who matter most, because a small merchant in peak week loses more than a large one on a Tuesday. A large share of "your platform is broken" is not our platform. Themes, apps, payment gateways and the merchant's own customisations sit inside the same page, so the real triage skill is proving where the fault lives quickly and without making the merchant feel handed off. The merchant does not experience an app boundary, and a technically correct refusal at that line is the most reliable way to lose them. The calendar is not ours. Peak trading, promotional launches and platform change freezes concentrate a quarter of the year's volume and the entirety of the year's stakes into weeks that are known a year in advance — which makes capacity a planning problem rather than a reactive one, and makes a freeze violation an incident on its own. The error carried in from B2B SaaS is scoping to our own code. The error carried in from consumer ecommerce is thinking in orders — here the unit in trouble is the merchant's whole storefront, and the shoppers behind it are a population we cannot contact.


## Characteristics

|  |  |
|---|---|
| requester | a merchant, their agency, or a developer building on our APIs — three requesters with different fluency and identical urgency |
| typical_resolution_hours | 12 |
| volume_shape | moderate baseline with extreme concentration at peak trading season and at every promotional event the merchant runs without telling us |
| staffing_model | tiered with a partner/agency channel and a separate merchant-success path for the largest storefronts |
| coverage | extended hours year-round, 24x7 through peak season and during declared change freezes |
| automation_level | moderate — status, order-lookup and setup questions deflect well; anything involving a third-party app does not |
| notes | typical_resolution_hours is low because so much of the queue is triage-to-correct-owner rather than end-to-end fix. That is a real property of the vertical and not a flattering metric — the merchant's problem often ends elsewhere.  |

## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.ticket`

Requires `product_area_ref`, `severity`, `priority`


> Product area has to distinguish our surface from a third-party one at intake, because that single fact determines whether this ticket can be resolved at all or only routed. Discovering it three replies in is where the merchant's patience is actually spent.


## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.incident`

Requires `is_customer_visible`, `blast_radius`, `status_page_published`


> Customer-visible has a second meaning here: visible to the merchant, or visible to the merchant's shoppers. The second is the one that generates the escalation, because the merchant is now failing in front of their own customers using our software.


## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.escalation`

Requires `severity_perceived`, `severity_assessed`


> These two diverge more here than anywhere else in B2B, and the divergence is usually the merchant being right. A merchant in peak week reporting a checkout error at a severity we assessed lower is not exaggerating; they are pricing it correctly and we are not.


## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.sla_target`


> Response targets that are comfortable in ordinary trading are indefensible in peak week. The clock does not change but its adequacy does, which is why breach_prevention here has to be read against the merchant's calendar and not against the contract alone.
